title: AD-16 audit keys missing from all_non_pii — the new schema-test arms added in this PR are vacuous and the documented registry invariant is silently broken
location: server/src/retention/audit_log_schema.gleam:87-88 (variants), :146-147 (to_string), :187-223 (all_non_pii — ends at RefSlot, no ReferenceCall entries); server/test/retention/audit_log_schema_test.gleam:92-93 (new case arms), :97 (iteration); audit writes at server/src/reference_checks/actions_handler.gleam:394-399
evidence: NonPiiKey gains OldReferenceCallId/NewReferenceCallId (audit_log_schema.gleam:87-88) and non_pii_to_string maps them to "old_reference_call_id"/"new_reference_call_id" (:146-147), but `all_non_pii` (const at :187-223) contains no ReferenceCall entries — grep of lines 187-223 returns zero matches for 'ReferenceCall'. The diff adds the two case arms `schema.OldReferenceCallId -> list.contains(schema.all_non_pii, k)` and `schema.NewReferenceCallId -> list.contains(schema.all_non_pii, k)` (audit_log_schema_test.gleam:92-93), but the runner is `list.each(schema.all_non_pii, fn(k) { non_pii_membership(k) |> should.be_true })` (:97) — it iterates the list itself, so the two missing keys are never visited and the arms never execute. The module header's step 3 documents 'Add the variant to all_pii / all_non_pii. The schema tests fail until you do' (audit_log_schema.gleam:11) — false here: the suite passes with the keys unregistered. The keys genuinely appear in audit_log.details: actions_handler.gleam:394-399 writes alog.non_pii(alog.OldReferenceCallId, ...) and alog.non_pii(alog.NewReferenceCallId, ...) in do_substitute's AD-16 audit.
detail: The registry's stated purpose is to be the 'Centralised registry of every key name that may appear in audit_log.details' — the two substitution-audit keys DO appear there but are absent from all_non_pii (and from all_pii, so no deny-list impact). Concretely broken: (1) all_non_pii_keys() omits the two keys — any future consumer of the registry gets an incomplete non-PII set; (2) the two test arms added by this PR assert membership that does not hold, and because they are never invoked they give false assurance that the AD-16 keys are registered. Verified at the worktree sha ace27b1: gleam check compiles the changed files, the full server unit suite is green (1476 passed / 512 integration skipped), and the arms are dead by construction, not by runtime failure. No production runtime impact today (all_non_pii has no production consumer), hence warning rather than blocker — but the new arms should either be backed by list entries or removed.
recommended_fix: Add OldReferenceCallId and NewReferenceCallId to the all_non_pii const (audit_log_schema.gleam:187) so the new test arms actually pin membership and all_non_pii_keys() reflects the registry; alternatively drop the two arms if the keys are intentionally unlisted.
